page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family. Virtualized on the KVM hypervisor, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs running on Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors with a nominal frequency of 3.4 GHz. Accompanying the processor cores is 64 GB of main memory, yielding an allocation of 4 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

The instance contains no integrated local storage, meaning that operational filesystems, operating system images, and database stores rely on cloud block storage volumes. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, facilitating reliable throughput for inter-service communication and distributed processing clusters. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default, which requires configuring elastic public IP resources or private network gateways for external access.

From an architectural perspective, the provision of dedicated 3.4 GHz clock speeds paired with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio targets workloads requiring low latency per instruction alongside multi-threaded throughput. Without local NVMe devices, I/O performance depends on network block storage sizing. The hardware configuration makes the instance suitable for computational modeling, microservices backends, batch processing, enterprise ERP systems, and web serving workloads where consistent CPU clock rates take precedence.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.4xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors running at a base clock frequency of 3.4 GHz. It includes 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present on the instance. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage. Networking capability includes a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. Due to its dedicated high-frequency cores and standard memory footprint, the instance balances single-threaded execution performance with parallel capability, making it suited for CPU-bound business applications, backend web services, compilation pipelines, and database deployments dependent on attached cloud block storage.
